summary: Sliced-batch reassembly strips pin header for chunked streamed multipart requests, causing silent fallback to legacy quantized variant
description:
Issue summary: Several enterprise tenants observed degraded output quality and unexpected model variant selection for requests that use multipart chunked uploads combined with streaming and function_call flags. The routing layer silently dropped the model pin metadata during reassembly, routing the request to a legacy quantized variant that fails to meet quality expectations.

Observed behavior: For large payloads split into chunked multipart boundaries, the reconstructed request reaching the serving runtime had no X-Model-Pin header in a subset of cases. Traffic routed to fallback path (legacy-quantized-v1) instead of the tenant's pinned model (gptx-3-large-fp16). Customer noticed poor completions and cost anomalies for affected sessions.
impact: 12 tenants affected (enterprise/dedicated), intermittent (~0.8% of chunked streaming requests in us-east), visible quality regressions for pinned model users, billing uptick for affected requests due to increased token generation and fallback processing. Customer support ticket volume increased from affected accounts. SLA risk for two enterprise customers.
environment: prod | us-east (primary), edge-proxy v2.3.1, api-gateway v1.9.4, serving-runtime (canary and stable pools)
steps_to_reproduce: Enable multipart chunked upload from client with chunk boundary markers and streaming=true and function_call provided in prompt metadata.
Pin tenant to model gptx-3-large-fp16 via tenant routing policy.
Send a large multipart request split across at least 3 chunks sized ~128KB each, ensure chunks align with client-side boundary token '---SLICE---'.
Observe request reassembly at edge-proxy and inspect headers forwarded to api-gateway/serving-runtime for presence of X-Model-Pin header.
If header missing, request is routed to fallback variant and quality/regression is reproducible.

investigation_notes: 2026-03-09 15:10 UTC - Initial triage by CS (Aisha Patel): identified correlation between chunked multipart uploads and missing X-Model-Pin header in forwarded requests.
2026-03-09 16:02 UTC - SRE (Jonah Kim): captured packet traces from edge-proxy and api-gateway, confirmed header present in first chunk but absent after reassembly in ~0.8% of samples.

2026-03-09 18:30 UTC - Eng (Samantha Ortiz): reproduced locally using synthetic client that mimics chunk boundary pattern; failure appears when chunk boundary aligns with internal buffer cut and when CDN (CloudFront) injects Transfer-Encoding: chunked in front.

Root cause hypothesis: edge-proxy v2.3.1 introduced a reassembly optimization that trims header metadata on chunk boundary splice to reduce memory copying. A race condition when metadata map is moved between buffer segments results in X-Model-Pin being dropped for certain boundary alignment cases.

Additional observation: requests that were not chunked or that used smaller chunk sizes did not reproduce the issue; streaming flag + function_call combination increases probability because both add streaming metadata that lives in headers and in body signals.

Mitigation applied (2026-03-10 02:00 UTC): temporary WAF header-insert rule to re-add X-Model-Pin for known affected tenant tokens arriving via edge-proxy; RBAC for header injection scoped to enterprise customers only. Reduced incidents for patched tenants.
Permanent fix in progress: PR open to edge-proxy to preserve header map across buffer splice operations and to add unit tests for reassembly boundary cases. PR link in related_github_prs.

Backfill plan: compute affected session tokens from logs (query request_id and tenant mapping) and reapply pin mapping to orchestrator routing table for open sessions within last 72 hours. Some short-lived sessions will not be recoverable and require customer follow-up.
Monitoring: additional telemetry added to routing layer to emit 'pin-presence' metric per request and boundary-alignment histogram to detect recurrence.

resolution: Hotfix merged to edge-proxy and rolled out to us-east. Temporary WAF header rewrite used as stopgap for enterprise tenants. Permanent fix includes preserving header metadata across buffer splices and adding boundary alignment test coverage. Backfill process to reapply pins for recoverable sessions initiated; CS outreach scheduled for unrecoverable cases. Monitoring and telemetry added. Closing when 48h stable with no recurrence and backfill complete.
